steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding
summary: AlignPred replaces storing raw or conventionally compressed persistent KV caches in multi-turn agent deployments with a codec that aligns heads/layers via local orthogonal transforms, predicts token-wise and cross-head/layer, then quantizes residuals on an error-bounded lattice with entropy coding, and it integrates with SGLang HiCache. The cost is added encode/decode compute in the serving path (CPU codec overhead, though reported as faster than baseline codecs), integration effort with a specific serving stack, and a configurable reconstruction-error budget that must be tuned per workload. Failure modes include quality degradation if the error budget is set too aggressively for tasks sensitive to KV fidelity, gains that may not transfer beyond the three evaluated attention mechanisms or the LongBench-Pro benchmark, and limited benefit for workloads without long-lived cross-session caches.
rationale: The method targets a real constraint (persistent KV storage for long-running agents) with a quantified storage reduction and an available SGLang HiCache integration, but the reader should validate the error-budget/quality tradeoff and codec overhead on their own models and workload before production adoption.
technique: Error-bounded KV cache codec with alignment and predictive coding

claims.statement: AlignPred replaces storing raw or conventionally compressed persistent KV caches in multi-turn agent deployments with a codec that aligns heads/layers via local orthogonal transforms, predicts token-wise and cross-head/layer, then quantizes residuals on an error-bounded lattice with entropy coding, and it integrates with SGLang HiCache. The cost is added encode/decode compute in the serving path (CPU codec overhead, though reported as faster than baseline codecs), integration effort with a specific serving stack, and a configurable reconstruction-error budget that must be tuned per workload. Failure modes include quality degradation if the error budget is set too aggressively for tasks sensitive to KV fidelity, gains that may not transfer beyond the three evaluated attention mechanisms or the LongBench-Pro benchmark, and limited benefit for workloads without long-lived cross-session caches.

Reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42-72% relative to native SGLang HiCache (a 1.7-3.6x storage factor) with comparable latency; decodes at least 1.6x faster than evaluated CPU codec baselines; near-native task scores on LongBench-Pro at 128K context.
